name: 2015 livery
description: White, with no cheatline: a dark Cathay green fin with a large white brushwing (a curved brush-stroke wing whose point faces forward) and a thin pale leading edge; 'CATHAY PACIFIC' in gray serif capitals over the forward windows and a small green brushwing under the cockpit. White engines, green sharklets with a pale leading edge.

sources.note: Cathay Pacific's own release on the livery unveiled in November 2015 (brushwing and name enlarged, name moved above the windows, all-green tail).

logos.description: The brushwing: a white calligraphic wing like a chevron pointing forward, its upper arm a long brush stroke curving up to a fine tip at the top near the trailing edge with ragged dry-brush edges, its lower arm short and straight back to a point at the fin's root by the trailing edge. Faces forward on both sides.
A small green brushwing under the cockpit windows, ahead of the first door, pointing forward.

titles.style: Classical serif capitals, regular weight, slightly spaced, upright, its baseline on the window tops, from just aft of the first door.

notes: Cathay's 2023 brand refresh (the group's master brand became 'Cathay', with a redrawn brushwing in its corporate identity) did not change the aircraft: 2025-2026 photos of new A321neos and A350s still show 'CATHAY PACIFIC' and this 2015 layout. Cathay's own description mentions a 'neat stripe of Cathay Pacific gray'; these photos show the lower fuselage only shading to gray, with no edge, so it isn't drawn: check against a clear photo of the belly. Not drawn: the registration and, in 2026, a small '80 years together' anniversary mark aft. A few airframes may still wear the pre-2015 scheme (gray belly, green and white cheatline, brushwing on a green fin with a white band); not checked. Measured on the A330-300 (the commonest type, 2026-11-15): on the A321neo and A350 the title is the same lettering, a little shorter as a share of the A350 and longer on the A321neo.
history: Replaced Skyarium v1's approximation. Unveiled on a 777-300ER in November 2015, replacing the 1994 brushwing scheme's gray belly and cheatlines; the fleet was repainted over the following five years.
